questions.text:
Let X be a square matrix. Consider the following two statements on X.

I. X is invertible
II. Determinant of X is non-zero

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
A square matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is non-zero ([latex]X^{-1}=\frac{adj(X)}{\det X}[/latex]). So I and II imply each other.

Answer: I and II are equivalent statements

questions.text: The domain of the function [latex]\log (\log \sin (x))[/latex] is:
questions.solution:
[latex]\sin x\le1[/latex], so [latex]\log\sin x\le0[/latex] wherever it is defined. The outer log needs a positive argument, which never happens. The domain is empty.

Answer: Empty set

questions.text:
Consider a matrix P whose only eigenvectors are the multiples of [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 4 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
Consider the following statements.
(I) P does not have an inverse
(II) P has a repeated eigenvalue
(III) P cannot be diagonalized
Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
A 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 matrix with only one independent eigenvector must have a repeated eigenvalue (II), and without 2 independent eigenvectors it cannot be diagonalized (III). The repeated eigenvalue can be any number, including a non-zero one, and then P is invertible; so I is not necessarily true.

Answer: Only II and III are necessarily true

options: Only I and III are necessarily true
Only I and II are necessarily true
Only II and III are necessarily true

questions.text: Consider a matrix [latex]A=uv^{T}\; where \; u=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2 \end{bmatrix},v=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]  Note that [latex]v^{T}[/latex]  denotes the transpose of v. The largest eigenvalue of A is _____.
questions.solution:
[latex]A=uv^T[/latex] has rank 1. [latex]Au=u(v^Tu)[/latex], so u is an eigenvector with eigenvalue [latex]v^Tu=1+2=3[/latex]; the other eigenvalue is 0.

Answer: 3

questions.text:
The value of [latex]\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}x\cos (x^{2})dx[/latex] correct to three decimal places
(assuming that [latex]\pi[/latex]  = 3.14 ) is
questions.solution:
Substitute [latex]u=x^2[/latex], [latex]du=2x\,dx[/latex]:
[latex]\int_0^{\pi/4}x\cos(x^2)dx=\frac12\sin(x^2)\Big|_0^{\pi/4}=\frac12\sin\left(\frac{\pi^2}{16}\right)=\frac12\sin(0.616)\approx\frac12(0.578)\approx0.289[/latex]

Answer: 0.289
